query: The Grafting Bench {On the grafting bench is the club's oldest experiment, a potted tree that bears pears on one branch and lemons on the other. Beside it, knives, twine, wax and an open invitation.|The grafting bench. Somebody's new graft has taken: a rose that grows on a gooseberry, looking pleased with itself.|The grafting bench. The two-fruit tree has a third branch now, and nobody will admit to it.} {The wax pot is warm and smells of honey.|A row of failed grafts stands along the back, each with a small apologetic label.|{season == "spring": Every graft on the bench is in bud.|The saplings are bare, and the twine shows.}} Try a graft of your own {You splice a cutting of mint onto a lavender root and wax it shut. A week later it's growing; it smells like a summer evening.|Your graft takes. Someone pins a label to it with your name and a small drawn star.|You graft a cutting onto the two-fruit tree itself. It takes, and the tree now has one branch that is entirely yours.} {The knife slips; so does the cutting. It joins the row of failures with its own small label, and you join the infirmary queue with a cut thumb.|Your graft sulks, browns and drops off within the week. Your thumb has a nick that takes longer to heal.|The twine won't hold and the wax burns your fingers. Your cutting goes to the failures' shelf.} Label the old grafts {You work out from the bark scars which graft went on when, and write it all down. The two-fruit tree is older than anyone thought.|You label the rose on the gooseberry, which turns out to be harder than growing it.|You map the two-fruit tree branch by branch. The third branch has no record at all. You write "unknown, but welcome".}
